title: Emergence of the genus Homo
summary: A jaw with teeth from Ledi-Geraru in Ethiopia establishes the presence of the genus Homo at 2.80 to 2.75 million years ago. It combines primitive traits seen in early Australopithecus with features found in later Homo. Later Homo habilis lived in eastern and southern Africa from 2.4 to 1.4 million years ago.

uncertainty.note: Start is the 2.80–2.75 Ma age of the Ledi-Geraru LD 350-1 mandible; end marks the transition to early Homo erectus and global Pleistocene dispersals by c. 1.8 Ma.

as_recorded.value: establishes the presence of Homo at 2.80 to 2.75 Ma

as_recorded.calendar: million years ago (Smithsonian Human Origins Program)

where.modern_name: Ledi-Geraru research area, Afar Regional State, Ethiopia (find spot of the oldest dated Homo fossil; early genus evolution spanned East and South African rift basins)
where.historical_name: Afar Depression, East African Rift System, late Pliocene; no polities existed

importance.justification: The origin of the genus Homo marks the founding of our own genus, initiating encephalization, stone tool cultures, and the lineage leading directly to Homo sapiens.

related.because: Australopithecus afarensis and related gracile australopiths represent the ancestral hominin stock from which early Homo diverged.
The evolutionary lineage of the genus Homo produced the speciation event of Homo sapiens in Africa.
The initial radiation of primates established the primate order within which hominins and Homo emerged.
Encephalization and dietary developments in early Homo fostered advanced subsistence strategies including controlled fire.
